app.name: Markbook
nav.label: Main
classes.title: My classes
classes.lede: Open a class to enter marks, publish assessments and write comments.
markbook.title: Markbook
markbook.lede: Select a mark to change it. The weighted percentage, the level and the class averages are worked out again when you save.
msg.unreachable: The mark could not be saved. Check your connection and try again.
msg.mark_invalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max}, or leave the box empty to clear the mark.
msg.stale: Maximum marks have changed since this page was opened. Reload the markbook before entering marks.
msg.bad_request: That request could not be understood.
export.body: To take these marks into a spreadsheet, select the markbook table, copy it and paste it into your spreadsheet. Weighted percentages and levels are worked out here and arrive as plain numbers, not formulas.
assess.publish_help: Students see published marks on their own page. Marks in a draft assessment are visible only to you.
msg.max_invalid: Enter a whole number of marks from 1 to 1000.
msg.max_below: A student already has {highest} marks in this assessment, so the maximum cannot be lower than {highest}.
msg.published: Published. Students can now see these marks.
msg.withdrawn: Withdrawn. Students can no longer see these marks.
msg.not_published: This assessment is not published, so there is nothing to withdraw.
msg.feedback_saved: Feedback saved. {name} can see it on their own page.
msg.feedback_choose: Choose a comment from the bank first.
field.private_note: Private note (only you can see this)
student.title: Your marks
student.provisional_help: Worked out from published marks only, so it can change as more work is marked.
student.no_marks: No marks have been published yet.
report.title: Levels report
report.lede: How many students are at each level. Only students with every mark in are counted.
help.title: Help
help.marks: Select a mark in the markbook, type the new mark and save it. Marks are whole numbers from 0 to the assessment's maximum; an empty box clears the mark. Change an assessment's maximum on its own page; it cannot be set below a mark a student already has.
help.rounding: Each mark counts towards the weighted percentage by its assessment's weight: Homework 20%, Quiz 20%, Project 30%, Exam 30%. The percentage is worked out exactly and shown to one decimal place, with halves rounded up. It appears once every assessment has a mark.
help.levels: Level 5 from 80%, level 4 from 70%, level 3 from 60%, level 2 from 50%, otherwise level 1, read from the percentage as shown.
help.publish: Students see an assessment's marks only once it is published, and stop seeing them if it is withdrawn. Their provisional percentage uses published marks only.
help.notes: Feedback chosen from the comment bank appears on the student's own page. A private note is for you alone and is never shown to the student.
missing.title: Page not found
missing.body: There is nothing at this address.
